three_d_prompt_drafts.title: Reference Frames, Distance and Displacement
three_d_prompt_drafts.prompt:
1. PURPOSE AND AUDIENCE
For middle and early high school physics students. The model should show that: (a) position is measured from an origin within a chosen reference frame (a coordinate system); (b) distance is the total length of the path travelled (a scalar); (c) displacement is the straight-line change in position from start to end, with a direction (a vector arrow); (d) a walking path of 3 grid squares east then 4 squares north gives a distance of 7 squares but a displacement of 5 squares (a 3-4-5 triangle); (e) motion depends on the reference frame: a passenger on a moving cart is at rest relative to the cart but moving relative to the ground observer.

2. OVERALL FORM
A flat square coordinate board with a walking route drawn on it and a small cart on a straight track along its front edge. Z is up. The board lies in the XY plane, centred at the origin, about 2 units across (-1 to +1 in X and Y). The best view is a three-quarter elevated view from the front-right (camera around (2.2, -2.4, 1.8) looking at the origin), so both the path triangle and the cart are visible. Use 1 grid square = 0.2 units.

3. PARTS
- ground_grid - thin square plate 2 x 2 x 0.02, top at z=0, light grey with thin darker grid lines every 0.2 units (lines can be a texture or thin raised strips joined into this one object).
- x_axis - red cylinder arrow (radius 0.012) along +X from the origin to x=0.95, cone tip; sits just above the grid (z=0.015). Optionally a short thin tail toward -X.
- y_axis - green cylinder arrow, same style, along +Y to y=0.95.
- z_axis - blue cylinder arrow, same style, straight up from the origin to z=0.6.
- origin_point - small white sphere (radius 0.04) at (0,0,0.02) where the three axes meet.
- ground_observer - simple stylised figure (capsule body + sphere head, ~0.25 tall), dark grey, standing at (-0.85, 0.75, 0) beside the board corner, facing the board; represents the person who owns the ground reference frame.
- start_marker - small flag: thin pole 0.18 tall with a green triangular flag, base at (-0.6, -0.4, 0).
- turning_point - small yellow disc/sphere (radius 0.035) at the corner of the route (0.0, -0.4, 0.02).
- end_marker - same flag style with a checkered or red flag, base at (0.0, 0.4, 0).
- path_leg_east - orange flattened tube or strip (width ~0.035) lying on the grid from (-0.6,-0.4) to (0.0,-0.4); length 0.6 = 3 squares. Add small chevrons or a tiny arrowhead showing direction east.
- path_leg_north - same orange strip from (0.0,-0.4) to (0.0,0.4); length 0.8 = 4 squares, arrowhead pointing north.
- displacement_arrow - bold purple 3D arrow (shaft radius 0.022, cone head) floating slightly higher (z=0.06) from the start point (-0.6,-0.4) straight to the end point (0.0,0.4); length exactly 1.0 = 5 squares. Head touches the end point.
- cart_track - two thin dark grey parallel rails along X from x=-0.95 to x=0.95 at y=-0.8 and y=-0.9 (just inside the front edge), on the grid.
- moving_cart - simple blue box cart (0.35 x 0.18 x 0.1) with four small black wheels, sitting on the track centred at (0.45, -0.85, 0.07).
- cart_reference_axes - a miniature set of axes (red X, green Y, blue Z, each ~0.15 long, thinner than the main axes) fixed to the cart's top rear corner, showing the cart has its own reference frame.
- cart_passenger - small figure like the observer (~0.15 tall), light blue, standing on the cart.
- cart_velocity_arrow - cyan arrow (~0.3 long) floating above the cart at z~0.35, pointing +X, showing the cart's motion relative to the ground.

4. INTERNAL STRUCTURE
No cutaway or transparency needed; everything is on or above the board surface. Keep the displacement arrow slightly raised so it does not merge with the grid.

5. ACCURACY NOTES
- Path legs must be exactly 0.6 and 0.8 long and perpendicular; displacement arrow exactly 1.0 long and must start at the start flag and end at the end flag (hypotenuse of the triangle).
- Path legs must connect end-to-end at the turning point with no gap.
- Start point is NOT at the origin, to show position is measured from the origin while displacement depends only on start and end.
- Axes follow the right-hand rule: X red, Y green, Z blue, meeting at the origin.
- Cart axes must be parallel to the main axes and attached to the cart.
- Separate each part into its own named object.

6. KEEP IT SIMPLE
No text labels, numbers, scenery, buildings or realistic people. Flat matte colours, smooth low-poly shapes. Clarity over realism.

parts.name: ground_grid
parts.label: Ground Grid
parts.description: A flat grid where each square is one unit of distance. It lets us measure positions and lengths in this reference frame.

parts.name: x_axis
parts.label: X Axis
parts.description: The red axis points east (positive x). Positions left or right of the origin are measured along it.

parts.name: y_axis
parts.label: Y Axis
parts.description: The green axis points north (positive y). Together with the x axis it gives every point on the ground a pair of coordinates.

parts.name: z_axis
parts.label: Z Axis
parts.description: The blue axis points straight up. A full 3D reference frame needs three perpendicular axes.

parts.name: origin_point
parts.label: Origin
parts.description: The zero point (0, 0, 0) of the reference frame. Every position is measured from here, and choosing a different origin changes the position numbers but not the displacement.

parts.name: ground_observer
parts.label: Ground Observer
parts.description: A person standing still on the ground. This observer uses the ground grid as their reference frame and sees the cart moving.

parts.name: start_marker
parts.label: Start Point
parts.description: Where the walk begins, 3 squares west and 2 squares south of the origin. Displacement is measured from this initial position.

parts.name: turning_point
parts.label: Turning Point
parts.description: The corner where the walker changes direction from east to north. Changing direction adds to distance but makes the path longer than the displacement.

parts.name: end_marker
parts.label: End Point
parts.description: Where the walk finishes. The displacement arrow ends here, at the final position.

parts.name: path_leg_east
parts.label: Path Leg: 3 Squares East
parts.description: The first part of the walk, 3 squares long. Its length counts toward the total distance travelled.

parts.name: path_leg_north
parts.label: Path Leg: 4 Squares North
parts.description: The second part of the walk, 4 squares long. Adding both legs gives a total distance of 7 squares, a scalar with no direction.

parts.name: displacement_arrow
parts.label: Displacement Vector
parts.description: A straight arrow from start to end, 5 squares long, pointing north-east. Displacement is a vector: it has size and direction and is never longer than the distance travelled.

parts.name: cart_track
parts.label: Cart Track
parts.description: Straight rails fixed to the ground. They guide the cart in a straight line along the x direction.

parts.name: moving_cart
parts.label: Moving Cart
parts.description: A cart rolling along the track. It can serve as a second reference frame that moves relative to the ground.

parts.name: cart_reference_axes
parts.label: Cart Reference Frame
parts.description: A small set of axes attached to the cart. Positions measured with these axes move along with the cart.

parts.name: cart_passenger
parts.label: Cart Passenger
parts.description: A rider standing on the cart. In the cart's frame the passenger is at rest, but in the ground frame the passenger is moving, showing that motion depends on the reference frame.

parts.name: cart_velocity_arrow
parts.label: Cart Velocity Arrow
parts.description: Shows the cart moving in the positive x direction as seen by the ground observer. Seen from the cart's own frame, the cart is not moving at all.

three_d_prompt_drafts.title: Motion in One Dimension: Cart, Motion Diagram and Graphs
three_d_prompt_drafts.prompt:
1. PURPOSE AND AUDIENCE
A review model for high-school or introductory physics students on motion in one dimension. It should connect three representations of one motion: a cart accelerating along a straight number-line track, a motion diagram of evenly timed snapshots, and the matching position-time and velocity-time graphs. Students should see that:
- displacement is a vector from the initial to the final position;
- velocity and acceleration are vectors along the line;
- equal time intervals with growing spacing mean acceleration;
- the slope of an x-t graph is velocity;
- the slope of a v-t graph is acceleration;
- the area under a v-t graph is displacement.
A small free-fall example shows that vertical motion is also 1D, with acceleration g pointing down.

2. OVERALL FORM
The scene is a tabletop diorama about 2 units across, centred at the origin, with Z up.
- The track runs along the X axis from x=-1 to x=1 at y=0, sitting on z=0.
- Two flat graph panels stand upright behind the track, side by side, at y=0.6.
- A small free-fall stand sits at the front right, near x=0.85, y=-0.55.
- Best view: from the front (negative Y), slightly above (about 25 degrees elevation), so the track, arrows and both graphs are visible together.
- Use a plain light-grey ground plate under everything.

3. PARTS
- track_position_axis: a long thin flat bar (2.0 x 0.12 x 0.03) along X, light grey, acting as a number line.
- tick_marks: thin dark-grey ticks every 0.2 units along the front edge of the track.
- origin_marker: a slightly taller black tick plus a small flat disc at x=0, labelled 0.
- positive_direction_indicator: a small white arrow at the right end of the track, pointing +X, with a '+x' plate.
- cart_initial_position: a semi-transparent pale-yellow cart (box about 0.14 x 0.1 x 0.07 with 4 small wheels) at x=-0.8.
- motion_diagram_ghosts: three faint grey translucent copies of the cart at x=-0.65, -0.4 and -0.05. These are equal time intervals; the spacing grows 0.15, 0.25, 0.35, 0.45.
- cart_final_position: a solid bright-yellow cart, same shape, at x=0.4.
- displacement_arrow: a green flat arrow just above the track at z=0.15, running from x=-0.8 to x=0.4.
- velocity_arrow_initial: a short blue arrow (length 0.1) above the initial cart at z=0.25, pointing +X.
- velocity_arrow_final: a longer blue arrow (length 0.5) above the final cart at z=0.25, pointing +X.
- acceleration_arrow: a red arrow (length 0.2) above the final cart at z=0.35, pointing +X. Same length as on every snapshot (constant acceleration).
- position_time_graph: an upright white panel (0.85 x 0.6) at x=-0.5, y=0.6, with black axes labelled t and x.
- position_time_curve: a dark-blue tube following an upward-curving parabola (concave up), rising more steeply to the right. Mark 5 dots at equal t steps matching the cart positions.
- tangent_slope_line: a short straight orange line touching the parabola at its last point, showing instantaneous velocity as slope.
- velocity_time_graph: an upright white panel, same size, at x=0.5, y=0.6, with axes labelled t and v.
- velocity_time_line: a straight blue tube from a small positive v at t=0 rising linearly; constant positive slope = acceleration.
- area_under_vt_line: a translucent green trapezoid filling the region between the line and the t-axis.
- free_fall_ball: a small red-orange sphere (radius 0.05) on a thin vertical grey post (height 0.6), with two faint ghost balls lower down and increasing spacing.
- gravity_acceleration_arrow: a red arrow pointing straight down (-Z) beside the ball, with a small 'g' plate.

4. INTERNAL STRUCTURE
No cutaway is needed. Make the ghosts and the initial cart about 30-40% opaque so the solid final cart stands out. The area fill should be about 50% opaque so the line stays visible.

5. ACCURACY NOTES
- Cart positions must follow constant acceleration: spacings increase by a constant amount each interval (0.15, 0.25, 0.35, 0.45).
- The displacement arrow must start exactly at the initial cart and end exactly at the final cart.
- The final velocity arrow is longer than the initial one. The acceleration arrow points in the same direction as velocity (speeding up).
- The x-t curve must be a parabola, concave up. The v-t graph must be a straight line, not curved. The v-t line starts above zero (nonzero initial velocity).
- The acceleration arrows on the ghosts are optional; if shown, they are all identical length.
- The gravity arrow points straight down. The falling-ball ghost spacing increases downward.

6. KEEP IT SIMPLE
- Leave out friction, forces, numbers on graph axes beyond the axis letters, and detailed cart mechanics.
- No text paragraphs; only the short labels named above.
- Use flat, clean materials and consistent colours: green = displacement, blue = velocity, red = acceleration.

parts.name: track_position_axis
parts.label: Position Axis (Track)
parts.description: A straight track acting as a number line. In one-dimensional motion, every position is just a number along this single line.

parts.name: tick_marks
parts.label: Tick Marks
parts.description: Evenly spaced marks that let you read positions along the axis, like a ruler.

parts.name: origin_marker
parts.label: Origin (x = 0)
parts.description: The reference point from which all positions are measured. Positions to the right are positive, to the left are negative.

parts.name: positive_direction_indicator
parts.label: Positive Direction
parts.description: Shows which way is chosen as positive. The sign of displacement, velocity and acceleration depends on this choice.

parts.name: cart_initial_position
parts.label: Initial Position
parts.description: Where the cart is at the start, at time t = 0. Its position is x initial.

parts.name: motion_diagram_ghosts
parts.label: Motion Diagram Snapshots
parts.description: Snapshots of the cart taken at equal time intervals. The gaps grow larger each interval, showing the cart is speeding up, which means it is accelerating.

parts.name: cart_final_position
parts.label: Final Position
parts.description: Where the cart is at the end of the time interval. Its position is x final.

parts.name: displacement_arrow
parts.label: Displacement
parts.description: The vector from the initial position to the final position, Δx = x final − x initial. It depends only on start and end points, not the path taken.

parts.name: velocity_arrow_initial
parts.label: Initial Velocity
parts.description: A short arrow showing the cart's velocity at the start. Velocity is the rate of change of position and has a direction.

parts.name: velocity_arrow_final
parts.label: Final Velocity
parts.description: A longer arrow showing the cart is moving faster at the end. The change in velocity over time is the acceleration.

parts.name: acceleration_arrow
parts.label: Acceleration
parts.description: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. It points in the same direction as velocity here, so the cart speeds up; it stays the same size because the acceleration is constant.

parts.name: position_time_graph
parts.label: Position-Time Graph
parts.description: A graph of the cart's position against time. Its slope at any moment equals the velocity.

parts.name: position_time_curve
parts.label: Position-Time Curve
parts.description: For constant acceleration the x-t graph is a parabola. It curves upward because the slope, the velocity, keeps increasing.

parts.name: tangent_slope_line
parts.label: Tangent Line (Instantaneous Velocity)
parts.description: A line touching the curve at one point. Its slope gives the instantaneous velocity at that moment.

parts.name: velocity_time_graph
parts.label: Velocity-Time Graph
parts.description: A graph of the cart's velocity against time. Its slope gives acceleration and the area under it gives displacement.

parts.name: velocity_time_line
parts.label: Velocity-Time Line
parts.description: A straight, rising line means velocity increases by the same amount each second. The constant slope is the constant acceleration.

parts.name: area_under_vt_line
parts.label: Area Under v-t Graph
parts.description: The shaded area between the line and the time axis equals the displacement of the cart during that time.

parts.name: free_fall_ball
parts.label: Free-Falling Ball
parts.description: A dropped ball moves in one dimension, vertically. Its snapshots spread out as it falls because it speeds up.

parts.name: gravity_acceleration_arrow
parts.label: Acceleration Due to Gravity (g)
parts.description: Near Earth's surface, a freely falling object accelerates downward at about 9.8 m/s² when air resistance is ignored, regardless of its mass.

circuit_labs.title: Moving plates and earthquakes
circuit_labs.instructions: Move the plates at different boundaries and watch what millions of years do: trenches, volcanoes, mountains, new ocean floor. Then look inside the Earth and follow earthquake waves through it.

circuit_labs.title: How do we breathe?
circuit_labs.instructions: Breathe in and out and watch the diaphragm, ribs and lungs. Then go for a run: change how fast and how deep you breathe to keep your blood oxygen up. Finally zoom into an alveolus and follow oxygen into the blood.

circuit_labs.title: Light the bulb
circuit_labs.instructions: Connect the battery to the bulb with wires so the bulb lights up. Then add the switch to the loop and use it to turn the bulb on and off. Try two bulbs in a row: what happens to the brightness?

circuit_labs.title: Float or sink?
circuit_labs.instructions: Drop different objects into the tank and change the liquid. Watch the forces, then drag the pressure probe down and see how pressure grows with depth.

circuit_labs.title: Planets, eclipses and seasons
circuit_labs.instructions: Run time and compare how long each planet's year is. Line up the Sun, Earth and Moon to make a solar and a lunar eclipse. Then tilt Earth and find out what really causes the seasons.

circuit_labs.title: Build water, carbon dioxide and methane
circuit_labs.instructions: Drag atoms onto the board and bond them. Every atom must have exactly the bonds it wants: H one, O two, C four. Look at the shape of each finished molecule.
